text:
maya: heads up — we need a proposal for surfacing SLO alert rules in the console. PMs want per-route thresholds and a way to cut down on pager noise. can we sketch options?

jon: 2 quick constraints: 1) different routes have wildly different lat distributions. 2) alert fatigue is real. defaults must be conservative.

maya: agreed. idea: default policy = non-paging notification for first 15min of marginal breach, then page on sustained >30m. allow teams to opt into immediate paging.

kevin: watch out for percentile choice. p95 might hide tail issues; p99 will blow up noise for some high-traffic routes. maybe surface both and let routing rules pick which metric to use.

maya: yeah — show p50/p95/p99 and error-rate together. default alert uses p95 + error-rate. UI can switch metric axis.

kevin: also suggest we support static thresholds AND relative (baseline+/-%). some regressions are relative.

sophia: +1 on baseline delta alerts. and we should expose an evaluation window (5m/1h/24h) so teams can tune sensitivity.

sam: from oncall POV: implement a noise filter that suppresses alerts when traffic is low or when rollout tag == canary. simple rules: if requests < 100/min, suppress paging and send a ticket.

maya: good. can we put these as knobs in a "SLO policy" panel in the route config? fields: metric, percentile, evaluation_window, breach_duration, notify_level, suppress_conditions.

jon: + show an example in JSON so infra and devex can iterate.

kevin: here's a quick config suggestion:

```json
{
  "slo_policy": "default",
  "metric": "latency",
  "percentile": 95,
  "threshold_ms": 450,
  "evaluation_window": "5m",
  "breach_duration": "15m",
  "notify_level": "page_on_sustained",
  "suppress": {
    "min_rps": 100,
    "rolling_deploy": true
  }
}
```

maya: perfect. UX question: how do we represent noise history? a toggle to show "alert chatter" graph (alerts/min) baked into the SLO page?

sam: yes — plus show recent suppressed alerts and why they were suppressed (low traffic, canary, duplicate route). that helps triage.

kevin: also expose "severity escalation" mapping to notification channels. e.g., minor -> slack channel, major -> pager, critical -> pager + sms. allow per-team overrides.

sophia: integrations: PagerDuty, Opsgenie, email, slack, and webhook. console should let teams test a rule (dry-run) that emits notifications to a sandbox endpoint. important for onboarding.

jon: implementation note: backend should store policies as immutable versions so rollbacks are auditable. and add a rate-limit on alert fanout to avoid downstream flood.

maya: agree on immutability. also add a "rollout window" flag so new policies can be gradually applied (canary percentage).

alerts-bot: [automated] sample alert: route=/v1/generate latency p95=980ms threshold=450ms duration=7m -> suppressed (canary=true)

maya: nice — that exact example should appear in suppressed list with link to request traces.

sam: last ask: default SLO templates per product (chat vs embeddings vs rerank have different baselines). avoid one-size-fits-all.

maya: okay action items: 1) kevin/sophia produce schema + API for policies (due EOD Fri). 2) sam/jon write suppression rules and oncall playbook. 3) devex to mock console panel (first pass next week).

jon: I'll add a note to the infra RFC to include immutable policy versions and fanout rate limits.

kevin: will PR the schema draft.

maya: thanks all :rocket:

sam: thanks.

alerts-bot: [automated] thread archived by bot (no activity for 72h)
